newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo sees up to 600,000 T '97 wheat surplus.
newsitem.headline: Yugo sees up to 600,000 T '97 wheat surplus.

text.p: Yugoslavia said on Friday it expected up to 600,000 tonnes of surplus from its 1997 wheat crop estimated at around three million tonnes.

"Yugoslavia needs up to 2.4 million tonnes of wheat to feed its population which leaves 500-600 thousand tonnes of surplus from this year's production," said Bajazit Pacariz of the fedral Agriculture Ministry.
Some two million tonnes of wheat was needed to secure enough bread for the country's 10.5 million population swollen with some half a million refugees, he told a news conference.
Another 250,000 tonnes are needed for seeds, 150,000 tonnes are used as fodder and 50,000 tonnes are the usual losses during harvesting and storage.
Pacariz said that final data say wheat has been sown on 817,600 hectares, or 235,000 ha more than in 1995. "But it is still below the all-time high of 854,000 ha," he added.

According to the latest estimates, the government expects a 2.93 million tonnes crop with an average yield of 3.58 tonnes per ha. Production on the state farms is seen at 762,000 tonnes and private farms are expected to yield 2.16 million tonnes.
Pacariz said some 28 million litres of fuel have been secured for 19,500 combines and around 10,000 other pieces of machinery employed in the harvest.
"Two million litres of fuel, alone, were secured for wheat-drying," he added.
The harvest was planned to last 15 days but rain and hailstorms have interrupted and slowed it down.
The production on 337,000 ha, or 41 percent of the total wheat area, reaped by July 17, stands at 1.27 million tonnes with an average yield of 3.76 tonnes per ha.
Nine days are needed to complete the harvest on the rest of 480,000 ha.

"Weather forecasters said the following week will be unstable with possible rainfalls so we have to use every hour to collect the crop even if the grain dampness exceeds by 15 percent," Miroslav Malesevic of the Novi Sad Institute for Wheat told Reuters by phone.
Only some 393,000 tonnes, or one-fourth of the expected production, has been stored by July 17, the Serbia's Agriculture Ministry said.
